result.title: Three Worlds for the Price of a Logarithm: Baseline-Protected Best-of-Both-Worlds Combinatorial Semi-Bandits
result.summary: Improving on a baseline requires exploring away from it, precisely where its performance may be lost. We propose DUET (Doubling Under Empirical Tests), a horizon-free phased mixing scheme for combinatorial semi-bandits with arbitrary finite action sets. Two observable tests decide when to double the learning weight and when to double the empirical-regret budget and restart. We instantiate the scheme with entropy-FTRL in mixed phases and hybrid-FTRL in pure phases. Assuming the baseline selects every arm with positive probability, this instantiation keeps expected baseline regret logarithmic in $T$, while its expected regret to every fixed action is $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ under non-anticipating adversarial losses and polylogarithmic, gap-dependent, under i.i.d. losses with a unique optimal action. All three guarantees hold at every deterministic horizon, and the algorithm knows neither the horizon, nor the gap, nor the environment type. Baseline protection, adversarial robustness, and stochastic adaptivity thus come from one scheme and two base learners, at the price of a logarithm.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 DUET：面向任意有限动作集的组合半臂赌博机的一种无时域（horizon-free）分阶段混合方案，用两个可观测检验决定何时加倍学习权重、何时加倍经验遗憾预算并重启；以 mixed 阶段 entropy-FTRL 与 pure 阶段 hybrid-FTRL 实例化后，在未知时域、未知 gap 与环境类型下同时获得对数级基线遗憾与次线性遗憾。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由可观测检验触发加倍或重启」的无时域自适应切换机制，可能为 LVR 中预算未知时的探索‑利用权衡、动态计算分配与 STOP/重启判据提供可核查的调度线索，但原文并非视觉或多模态推理研究。
